recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-21230 unless a future work group decision changes the broader relative-reference policy.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-core issue asking that inconsistent guidance around relative URL format be fixed so Reference.reference uses "Patient/123" rather than "/Patient/123" for the RESTful relative reference structure.
initial_application: Jira records the issue as applied in commit 1d7085a and PR HL7/fhir#1959. Git commit 1d7085a2c6cde0781eddfb7692790c6475e3b577 changed source/datatypes/reference.xml from structure "/[type]/[id]" to "[type]/[id]"; PR merge de7092273be01dca22361a90a284c5dd75fb24b3 brought that application into the main history.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists Reference as a datatype and maps the reference datatype page to references, confirming source/datatypes/reference.xml is in current build scope for the definitions page. The cited Zulip thread records agreement that relative URLs should not start with a slash. Later Bundle reference-resolution wording from FHIR-29271 also uses "[type]/[id]" and has already been reconciled separately on the combined branch, so it supports consistency but was not decided here.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current authoritative Reference source already has the requested no-leading-slash structure, and a targeted search of source/datatypes/reference.xml, source/references-definitions.html, and source/references.html found no remaining old structure "/[type]/[id]" phrase.

related_jiras.note: Later Bundle reference-resolution clarification uses the same "[type]/[id]" relative-reference form; it is already represented by a separate combined-branch reconciliation commit and was used only as supporting context.
